summary: Iteration 3 — validated the 4 new features (category cleanup, CVI enrichment, bulk import, favourites) plus regression. Backend: 18/18 pytest passed (9 new iter3 + 9 existing). GET /api/analytes returns 378 built-in analytes, ~19 clinical panels, zero matrix-named categories. Enrichment: 95+ analytes are detailed with specs/peer_sigma (Homocysteine now enriched via _SUPP). POST /api/analytes/import works for CSV (header auto-detect with CVI/CVG => detailed=true), CSV positional (matrix,name,tea), and XLSX (openpyxl). DELETE /api/analytes/custom returns db to 378. Regression math intact (TEa 6.96/CV 1.4/Bias 1.1 => sigma 4.19). Frontend: Database category filter lists 20 clinical panels (no Serum/Plasma/Urine); starring Glucose persists to localStorage['sigmalab_favourites'] and pins to top of list; Import dialog accepts CSV, success toast fires, row appears with 'IMPORTED' tag; clear-imported button removes them; Calculator dropdown shows Glucose first (favourites-first). Iter2 test peer_sigma_range updated to skip non-detailed analytes (peer_sigma may be None for 280+ EFLM-only analytes).
critical_code_review_comments: Duplicate analyte names: Calculator dropdown shows two 'Glucose' entries (detailed from _RAW + one from EXTENDED_TEA with TEa 5.5%). Consider deduping by normalized name in build_database() or the frontend select — favourites match by name so both duplicates would star together.

classify() first-match keyword order: 'test' triggers 'Hormones'? No — but 'Semen Analysis' rule with keyword 'test' would misclassify anything containing 'test'. Actually _CATEGORY_RULES uses 'spermatozoa'/'semen' for Semen, so safe. But keyword 'anal' in Enzymes/Hormones vocabulary is potentially triggered by CSV header word 'Analyte' during positional detection (already handled by _parse_rows header auto-detect). Non-blocking.
biological_variation.py: no dedup between _RAW and EXTENDED_TEA — leads to duplicate 'Glucose' etc. in /api/analytes response.
Import endpoint has no size/row limit; a huge file could bloat db.custom_analytes.
